artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonnegative integer $n$ and an indeterminate $x$, define the Delannoy polynomial
$$D_n(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}^{2}x^{k}(x+1)^{n-k}.$$
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $x$ be an integer with $x\not\equiv 0,-1\pmod p$. Prove or disprove the following two congruences:
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(2k+1)(-1)^{k}D_{k}(x)^{3}\equiv p\left(\frac{4x+1}{p}\right)\pmod{p^{2}},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(2k+1)D_{k}(x)^{4}\equiv p\pmod{p^{2}},$$
where $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denotes the Legendre symbol.

Status could not be definitively verified.

status_evidence.title: Zhi-Wei Sun, Supercongruences involving Delannoy and related polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Defines D_n(x) and studies congruences modulo p^2 of sums involving (2k+1)D_k(x)^m.
status_evidence.claim: Sun's framework defines the Delannoy polynomials and contains many open congruence conjectures of this form.

status_evidence.title: Supercongruences using modular forms
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper proving certain Sun-type supercongruences via modular forms.
status_evidence.claim: Some Sun supercongruences have been resolved by modular form methods, but the specific cubic and quartic D_k(x) sums above are not addressed there.
